PullRequest.Title: Enable execution subagent by default with GPT-5.6 Luna
PullRequest.Body:

Changes only the execution subagent defaults in the extension manifest and runtime configuration:

- Enable the execution subagent by default.
- Use `gpt-5.6-luna` as its default model.

No test, description, or other behavior changes are included. Existing user and experiment overrides remain unchanged.

**Validation**

- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `git diff --stat upstream/main` - confirmed the PR changes only four default values across two files.
- Tests were not rerun for this defaults-only revision.

**How to test manually**

With a Copilot-backed agent session and no execution-subagent setting overrides, confirm the Execution Subagent tool is available and uses GPT-5.6 Luna. Manual UI verification was not run.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The default-to-tool-availability path, imperative routing text, awaited nested loop, single exposed terminal tool, and one-request-per-loop-iteration behavior are all explicit in code. Exact added milliseconds and how consistently each parent model obeys the routing instruction vary by model, which limits severity rather than confidence in the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: serialized model API requests and their prompt/completion token processing
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every terminal-oriented agent task that follows the now-default executionSubagent guidance, the cost grows with the nested loop's model iterations (up to the configured 10 calls); even one known command requires a subagent request to emit run_in_terminal and another to consume its result and emit the final answer.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased end-to-end latency and model/network work before command results reach the user
Findings.PreviousBehavior: With the default false, execution_subagent was absent from the parent agent's available tools. A request such as running one test command could use run_in_terminal directly, then make the normal parent follow-up model request after the command completed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: With the default true, the tool is exposed and its modelDescription explicitly says to use it instead of individual run_in_terminal calls and lists running tests as an example. Invocation awaits ExecutionSubagentToolCallingLoop.run(); that loop makes a model request to select run_in_terminal and, because ToolCallingLoop continues after a tool call, another model request to read the terminal result and produce <final_answer>, all before the parent loop can continue.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Changing the contributed setting default to true makes execution_subagent available for users without overrides; the matching runtime default at configurationService.ts:795 causes getAgentTools() to include it on CAPI agent requests, whereas the previous false defaults excluded this path.
Findings.Title: Keep single commands on the direct terminal path
Findings.Impact: Common prompts such as “run the tests” or “run this command” can wait for two additional model round trips before showing a final result, even when the command is already known and needs no orchestration; multi-step executions can add further nested requests up to the 10-call limit.
Findings.Evidence: package.json:182-207 defines execution_subagent with the imperative `USE THIS INSTEAD OF RUNNING INDIVIDUAL COMMANDS WITH run_in_terminal` and a run-tests example. agentIntent.ts:249-266 includes it when ExecutionSubagentToolEnabled is true. executionSubagentTool.ts:115 awaits loop.run(). executionSubagentToolCallingLoop.ts:347-363 exposes only run_in_terminal, and :366-390 sends each nested iteration through endpoint.makeChatRequest2. ToolCallingLoop._runLoop at toolCallingLoop.ts:1465-1495 repeats after any response containing a tool call, so a successful one-command execution needs one nested request to issue the command and a second to summarize its result. These requests are serialized around the terminal operation and then the parent still resumes its own loop.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the tool enabled, but remove the blanket routing instruction and direct the parent to use run_in_terminal for a single known command; reserve execution_subagent for genuinely iterative command discovery or output-reduction tasks where the extra model round trips replace comparable parent-agent iterations.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ordinary CAPI agent turn where the execution subagent is available but not selected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The parent request runs getAgentTools, token-counts all enabled schemas, serializes them into requestOptions.tools, and waits for the existing parent model request. The diff adds the execution_subagent definition to that request by default but does not start its implementation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parent agent model request containing enabled tool definitions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing request per parent loop iteration; the diff adds one bounded tool description/schema to each request rather than adding another request in this scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same parent request occurred without the execution_subagent schema under the false default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The parent model request is already critical-path; the additional schema adds bounded serialization/token processing and payload size.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of parent agent loop iterations; one additional fixed-size tool schema is processed per iteration.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Prompt construction, token counting, and the parent fetch are sequential within each loop iteration. No new concurrent work is launched merely by exposing the tool.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The schema can participate in provider prompt caching and is marked non-deferred, but it remains included and token-counted on each request. There is no cold-start construction or invocation of the subagent until selected.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: getAgentTools gating, tool-token counting, request serialization, and non-deferred classification are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact schema-token and wire-size overhead depends on endpoint serialization and provider caching; it is bounded to one tool and is not independently severe enough to report.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding. This is bounded serialization overhead inherent in exposing one tool, not a high-impact regression by itself.

Scenarios.Scenario: Single known terminal command such as running one test command
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The parent model selects execution_subagent, then ExecutionSubagentTool.invoke awaits endpoint resolution and the nested loop. The nested model must first emit run_in_terminal; after that subprocess completes, a second nested model request consumes the result and emits final_answer. Only then does the parent loop resume and make its normal follow-up request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Nested execution-subagent model requests through endpoint.makeChatRequest2
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least two serialized nested model calls for one successful command: one to issue run_in_terminal and one to summarize its result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With the tool disabled by default, the parent could issue run_in_terminal directly, execute the command, and proceed to its normal follow-up model request without the two nested model calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both requests block return from execution_subagent and therefore delay the parent response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute the requested command via run_in_terminal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One subprocess/tool invocation for the realistic single-command case.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The parent agent could invoke the same terminal tool directly once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command remains critical-path in both paths; the diff wraps it with nested model requests rather than increasing this subprocess count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve all CAPI model metadata when selecting gpt-5.6-luna
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getAllChatEndpoints call per subagent instance; its model fetch is normally cache-backed and can issue one /models request when cold or older than ten minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Default-disabled users never entered this resolution path; explicitly enabled users already resolved the configured execution model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Endpoint resolution is awaited before the nested loop; on a warm model cache it is in-memory, while a cold refresh can add one request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One occurrence per terminal-oriented parent task routed to the tool. Added model calls scale with nested iterations; the configured loop permits up to 10 tool calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The parent awaits the entire subagent; nested model request, terminal command, and summary request are serialized. The prompt explicitly prohibits parallel terminal calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Endpoint discovery coalesces and caches model metadata for ten minutes. The nested model requests themselves are not coalesced because each depends on the preceding tool result; provider prompt caching may reduce input processing but cannot remove their network round trips.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the default gating, routing instruction, awaited nested loop, one model fetch per loop iteration, and continuation after tool calls are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on parent-model tool choice, endpoint response time, and command duration. The imperative tool description and run-tests example make the trigger realistic, while duration variability supports medium severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported as a medium boundary-fanout regression because common single-command tasks gain two avoidable serialized model round trips.

Scenarios.Scenario: Iterative multi-command execution through the execution subagent
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The parent blocks while the nested loop alternates model requests with run_in_terminal calls until final_answer or the tool-call limit, then resumes its own loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execution-subagent model request per nested iteration
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized model request per nested iteration, supporting up to 10 terminal tool calls plus a final-answer iteration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The default path did not expose this nested loop; iterative work remained in parent-agent rounds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every nested request is on the parent response critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sequential run_in_terminal commands selected by the nested model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to the configured 10 tool calls, one terminal call per turn by prompt policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Comparable iterative tasks could also run multiple terminal commands in parent-agent rounds; the diff changes orchestration and adds the nested model layer rather than proving higher subprocess cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous commands block each subsequent nested model iteration; timed-out/background commands terminate further tool exposure.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of commands and nested iterations, bounded by the 10-tool-call setting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Strictly serial: the prompt says one run_in_terminal per turn and the loop awaits each model and tool result. Background/time-out handling removes tools and forces finalization rather than creating a burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The selected endpoint is memoized within one subagent loop. Model metadata is shared/cached for ten minutes; dependent nested responses cannot be coalesced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for serialization and bounds; relative latency versus parent-only orchestration varies by task.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: For genuinely iterative tasks, the compact execution model may replace similarly many parent rounds and could be beneficial; no additional finding is made beyond the clearly worse single-command case.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding because multi-step tasks may trade nested requests for equivalent parent iterations, and subprocess fan-out is bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Execution-subagent model changes from gemini-3-flash to gpt-5.6-luna
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On invocation, resolveEndpoint reads the new default, resolves model metadata, and all nested fetches use the selected endpoint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve model metadata and issue nested requests to the selected model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached endpoint resolution per subagent instance and the same number of nested model calls as before for already-enabled users.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Already-enabled users used gemini-3-flash for the same endpoint-resolution and nested-loop structure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Resolution and model responses are awaited, but the model-name change does not alter request count or concurrency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Nested iteration count, unchanged by the model string.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Endpoint metadata follows the existing ten-minute model cache and per-loop endpoint promise memoization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that boundary cardinality is unchanged; low evidence for any model-specific performance delta.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No repository evidence establishes that gpt-5.6-luna is slower, more expensive, or uses more memory than gemini-3-flash for this workload.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding; a model-name substitution alone does not prove a performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Extension activation with the new setting default
Scenarios.CriticalPath: VS Code evaluates the contributed languageModelTools `when` clause and the Copilot extension imports/registers tool implementations. The implementation module was already imported unconditionally through allTools, so the setting change does not newly construct the nested loop or resolve a model during activation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one additional enabled contribution; no collection or lifetime growth was found.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No changed asynchronous work or background queue is started at activation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No changed cache allocation or retained-key lifecycle was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from unconditional allTools import, static ToolRegistry registration, and lazy loop construction inside invoke.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Contribution-registry bookkeeping is not quantified, but no new filesystem, subprocess, IPC, database, or network boundary is reached until invocation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and their full diffs. One medium boundary-fanout issue was submitted for default routing of simple terminal tasks through an awaited nested model loop. Checked startup eagerness, schema serialization, prompt caching, endpoint-model caching, subprocess cardinality, concurrency bounds, and the model-name change; no other high-confidence diff-caused performance regression or regression fix was established.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
